Anotei 80: (continuation) the power of speech. Now I move
81	the power of speech. Now I move
82	from the Torah to the Writings, in the book of Kohelet, King Solomon.
83	In the book of Kohelet, chapter 5, he addresses the matter of
84	vows. Remember in the background the words we started from,
85	from our Parashah: "When you vow a vow to HaShem, do not delay
86	to pay it." And here now Kohelet chapter 5: "When you vow
87	a vow to God, do not delay to pay it." We see that this is
88	exactly the same, really a repetition of what
89	is written in the verse in the book of Devarim: "When you vow a vow
90	to God, do not delay to pay it." King Solomon continues
91	and says: "for He has no pleasure in fools; pay what you vow."
92	He has no pleasure in fools. A fool is one who says
93	and does not fulfill, or who at the time he spoke did not
94	intend to fulfill, or who at the time he spoke did intend to,
95	and afterward it simply melted away and he did not carry
96	it out. This is called foolishness. "He has no pleasure in fools; pay
97	what you vow." And if you remember that verse
98	in the Torah, "But if you refrain from vowing, there will be no
99	sin in you." So the next verse here is very similar:
100	"Better that you not vow than that you vow and not pay." It is better
101	not to vow at all, do not vow any vow. But if
102	you do vow, pay. So "better that you not vow at all
103	than that you vow and not pay." Now he adds: "Do not let
104	your mouth cause your flesh to sin."
105	If you take an obligation upon yourself and you do not
106	fulfill it, then you will suffer a loss here: causing to sin
107	is a loss, causing your flesh to sin. "Do not
108	let your mouth" — that is, the mouth has power, and it can,
109	if
110	you do not carry out what you said, it can bring you
111	harm to the body. "Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin,
112	and do not say before the angel that it was an error": you cannot
113	apologize and say "I did not mean it," and so on. "Why
114	should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?"
115	All of you. So again we have here another reference
116	to speech, voice: from the moment a person says something, it
117	is binding, even between man and his fellow, every commitment,
